learningObjective: Distinguish real benefits and limits of continuous batching from common overclaims.

canonicalClaims.claim: Continuous batching removes head-of-line blocking under variable-length outputs and boosts aggregate throughput; per-request TPOT does not decrease vs solo execution and can slightly increase due to shared-batch interference.
nonImplications: Does not help a single-request workload.

misconceptions.whyWrong: It improves throughput and fairness, not per-request latency.

misconceptions.claim: Continuous batching applies only to MoE models.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Dense models are the primary beneficiaries.

misconceptions.claim: Continuous batching requires per-request CUDA streams.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The mechanism is scheduling granularity; requests share a single batched forward.

implementationFacts: vLLM, TRT-LLM, SGLang all implement continuous batching as core functionality.
Combined with chunked prefill, continuous batching also handles prefill/decode interleaving.
performanceScenarios: The larger the output-length variance, the larger the throughput improvement over static batching.
